QuickHacks are NET Actions performed against Neuroports after all Passwalls have been successfully Breached.

A Netrunner may only attempt one QuickHack per target per Turn.

All Neuroports possess built-in firewall security.

Netrunners with Interface Rank 1-2 must succeed at a DV6 Interface Check before attempting to establish a QuickHack connection.

Netrunners with Interface Rank 3+ bypass this security automatically.

Failure does not alert the target.

If the Netrunner is forcefully removed from the Neuroport they are considered to have Unsafely Jacked Out.

After being Unsafely Jacked Out, the Netrunner may not attempt to reconnect to that target for 60 minutes.

QuickHacks target a user's Neuroport architecture.

A Neuroport acts as a NET Architecture containing Passwalls, Control Nodes and borrowed Black ICE.

Black ICE installed on an active Cyberdeck may be used by the Neuroport.

Netrunners are always considered Jacked Into their own Neuroport and may immediately respond to hostile intrusions.

A successful QuickHack causes the target to become aware that their Neuroport has been compromised unless the QuickHack specifically states otherwise.

A Netrunner may use Interface Plugs to establish a direct connection to a target's Neuroport.

Awake targets automatically become aware of the intrusion.

While directly connected:

  • Gain +1 NET Action.
  • Ignore Passwalls.
  • Black ICE remains active.

If either participant moves more than one square apart, the connection is broken and the Netrunner is Unsafely Jacked Out.

ConfigurationRange
External Cyberdeck3 Squares
External Cyberdeck + Range Upgrade4 Squares
Neuroport Cyberdeck Port25 Squares

Line of sight is required for all QuickHacks.

Self-ICE is specialized Neuralware designed to resist QuickHacks.

Each Self-ICE installation adds one Passwall to the user's Neuroport architecture.

Maximum installations: 3.
